speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
text: asked	the Minister for Transport how the plan for a cashless public transport system by 2020 will ensure that the elderly who rely on cash as their sole mode of payment will not be left out.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked	 the Minister for Transport (a) what are the consultations that LTA has conducted prior to announcing the plan for a cashless public transport system by 2020; and (b) of the consultations which took place, what proportion of members of the public consulted were senior citizens.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked	the Minister for Transport what is the estimated annual cost of maintaining existing cash transaction capabilities in our public transport system.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked	 the Minister for Transport how will the Ministry make it easier for commuters to top up their EZ-Link card at MRT stations, bus interchanges, convenience stores and to use cardless payment via QR codes and remotely via the Internet.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: However, two out of three commuters top up their cards with cash.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Topping-up with cash is cumbersome for the commuter as he has to queue up to withdraw cash, then queue up again to top up the card.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Our aim is for commuters, including tourists, to avoid the hassle of doing cash top-ups.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In fact, they should not need a Specification for Contactless e-Purse Application (CEPAS) card for transport payments.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: From June 2018, we will extend the pilot to VISA and NETS 2.0 holders.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: ABT will eventually be fully rolled out to the entire public transport system.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: For commuters who continue to use CEPAS cards, we will make electronic top-ups more convenient.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: They will be able to top up their travel cards online, through General Interbank Recurring Orders (GIRO) or using their mobile phones.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will also be able to top up our children or senior parent's travel cards easily.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We are challenging LTA and TransitLink to make ABT and electronic top-ups so convenient for commuters that cash top-ups and payments will become the less preferred option.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will manage the transition gradually over several years, so that no commuter needs to feel left out.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will focus attention on the small minority of commuters who need further assistance.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA and TransitLink are geared up to help.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We are also working closely with other agencies, such as the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), to make e-payments more accessible to all, including those who do not have bank accounts, which is the case for some foreign workers.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: An e-payment based public transport system is an important initiative to make life easier for all commuters.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We have consulted widely across a number of demographic groups.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will continue to widen and deepen stakeholders' engagements.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The first question is, for ABT, which countries have so far deployed this and what are some of the learning points that we have taken on board to smoothen the adoption and, certainly, how do we bring the seniors who may not be so IT-savvy on board?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: In addition to cost savings, there will also be manpower resource savings as well.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Staff of the Public Transport Operators (PTOs) who are currently providing ticketing services at rail stations will be freed up to better concentrate on their core duties in rail operations.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The cost savings can also be channelled to hiring service agents in educating elderly commuters in this cashless journey and also to produce educational materials.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As to whether the eventual cost savings will be passed on to commuters, we will have to look at the PTOs' profit and loss eventually.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As to ABT, this is a pilot project that has been introduced just at the beginning of this year.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We have started with MasterCard, we will be implementing it together with VISA and NETS next year.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I am not aware whether there are any countries that are using this system.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Nonetheless, we will be sourcing around to see what the best practices are and implement them whenever necessary.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I have got two supplementary questions for the Senior Minister of State for Transport.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Yes, LTA and Transit Link have engaged advisors as well as grassroots organisations of the areas where the 11 passenger service centres would be ceasing cash top-ups from 1 September 2017.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: All in all, 29 constituencies were engaged and, out of about 300 participants consulted, about 30% were seniors.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: LTA has conducted a series of focus group discussions, face-to-face discussions across a representation of respondents, including senior citizens, so that we can better understand their concerns and feedback.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Out of 120 participants, about 25% were seniors.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We are pretty encouraged by the responses and support given and will continue to monitor the feedback closely as we progressively roll out some of these new initiatives.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will also continue to widen and deepen engagement of various stakeholders.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As to the Member's second question on cost savings, we will take these suggestions seriously and we will convey them to LTA and Transit Link to hire more service agents who can engage all the senior citizens more effectively.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: For the second question, will MOT explore allowing commuters to pay MRT and bus fares using Apple or Android Pay via their mobile phone?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: The third supplementary question: for existing means of cashless top-ups, commuters typically need to have a bank account but some Singaporeans do not have bank accounts.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Even if they have a bank account, they do not have enough money to maintain a minimum cash balance of $500 or $1,000.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: So, I hope MOT can work with MAS to ensure that every Singaporean can have a savings account that does not need to maintain a minimum balance without attracting any bank charges.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: A high proportion of Singaporeans, including the seniors, have bank accounts and this is also based on information that we gathered from the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Voucher scheme where only a small proportion of Singaporeans encashed their cheques received under the GST scheme, which could be an indicator that those who did so may not have a bank account.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Some banks also provide the service free for school-going children, the elderly and for those on public assistance by waiving the account service fees.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: However, we understand that many elderly may not be aware of these services, and MOT and MAS will work with the industry as well as with grassroots organisations to reach out to this group of elderly and to help them to transit and adapt to the e-payment options.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Alternatively, family members can also help top up for these seniors via online or mobile apps.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With regard to the Member's supplementary question on the transaction fee, we have to take this back to take a look and to discuss it with the various agencies.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: However, I would like to conclude that the world is changing very fast, technological advancement and innovative solutions are introduced incessantly.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: While they can make lives more convenient and efficient for many, they also disrupt the lives of some.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As a nation, we need to embrace such technological changes and ride on the positive impact that they can bring to our lives.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Further procrastination will only delay the problem and make catching up even more challenging.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: So, the best way to not leave anyone behind is to take the extra effort to bring everyone along this journey.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I can assure the Members that the Government will do its best to facilitate it.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I think there is one more group we also need to reach out to, and I am wondering whether MOT will be working with the Ministry of Manpower to reach out to the foreign workers, many of whom actually do not have bank accounts.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: This is another group that we will try to facilitate as much as possible.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will be working with the banks and MAS to see how we can facilitate the opening of bank accounts for this group of commuters.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: At the same time, I have also mentioned in my replies just now that for those commuters who really cannot switch to e-payments, there will still be cash alternatives at sites that are nearby to the transport modes.
